body.x: “Neurélux is a non-contact brain healthcare solution designed to help manage Alzheimer’s disease (dementia) and sleep disorders—key challenges in an ultra-aging society—within everyday life.”

This single statement delivered by Korea Lighting at CES 2026 clearly illustrated the direction in which the brain healthcare market is heading. Brain health management, once confined to hospitals and clinical settings, is now shifting into everyday living spaces. At the center of this transition is a key concept: non-contact technology.

During CES 2026, Korea Lighting unveiled Neurélux, a light-therapy-based brain health management solution, and simultaneously signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MTech Lab, a medical technology company involving faculty from the College of Medicine at Gachon University, to pursue clinical validation. The move drew significant attention, as it signaled a direct leap beyond product demonstration into the next phase—clinical testing and data-based verification.

body.x: Choosing “Non-Contact”: A New Standard in Brain Healthcare, Targeting Dementia

Neurélux is a non-invasive, non-contact brain healthcare device that utilizes specific wavelengths of light to influence brain function without physical contact or mechanical stimulation. Designed in a form factor similar to a conventional lighting stand, the device allows users to experience light therapy naturally within everyday spaces—without the need for wearing, pressure, or physical attachment. This design makes it particularly suitable for elderly users and environments requiring long-term use.

Technologically, Neurélux is built on a dual near-infrared wavelength structure. The 810nm wavelength activates mitochondria within brain cells, promoting ATP (cellular energy) production and supporting neuroprotection and recovery—mechanisms that are drawing attention in neurodegenerative conditions such as dementia. The 1,064nm wavelength penetrates deeper brain tissue, improving cerebral blood flow and supporting neuroplasticity to help maintain cognitive function.

Korea Lighting defines this approach as “Ambient Brain Healthcare.” Rather than treating brain health as a clinical procedure confined to hospitals, it reframes care as an environmental element embedded in daily life. This concept extends beyond dementia prevention and cognitive care for older adults to include modern individuals experiencing sleep disturbances or cognitive fatigue. Neurélux proposes a new standard: creating an environment where brain health can be managed continuously and naturally as part of everyday living.

body.x: "The Technology Is Ready—Now It Must Be Proven Clinically"

At CES 2026, Korea Lighting placed particular emphasis on clinical validation. Rather than relying on subjective experiences or explanatory claims, the company aims to verify Neurélux’s effects through MRI-based data analysis. MTech Lab, the clinical partner in this effort, specializes in AI-based MRI image analysis and has developed solutions targeting early detection of brain diseases such as dementia. The collaboration clearly targets what comes after product development—the stage that determines market trust.

“MTech Lab possesses technology that enhances MRI image quality and quantitatively analyzes brain changes using AI,” said Hyun-man Baek, CEO of MTech Lab, at the MOU signing ceremony. “Our core objective in this collaboration is to validate changes before and after Neurélux use through data, and to accumulate scientific evidence via long-term clinical studies.” He added, “Presenting invisible changes—such as cerebral blood flow and tissue responses—in numerical and visual form is the true starting point of clinical validation.”

Korea Lighting echoed this sentiment. Dong-woo Lee, CEO of Korea Lighting, emphasized, “No matter how advanced a technology is, in healthcare it is impossible to gain market trust without clinical validation.” He continued, “This MOU represents the process of building a scientific foundation to explain the value of Neurélux. Through clinical data, we aim to clearly demonstrate its efficacy and move toward a stage where global healthcare companies can confidently consider collaboration.”

body.x: “Clinical Validation Is the Starting Point of Market Trust”… Global Collaboration Potential Emerges

At CES 2026, Neurélux was recognized not merely as a consumer product, but as a collaboration-ready technology platform attracting interest from global healthcare companies. Current global healthcare trends are converging around four key directions: ▲ non-invasive and non-contact approaches ▲ application in everyday living spaces ▲ wellness-oriented management designed for long-term use ▲ data-driven verification of effectiveness. Demand is growing rapidly, particularly in sleep management, cognitive maintenance, and aging-related healthcare, for technologies that enable continuous use without physical burden.

Neurélux aligns closely with these trends. Its non-contact light therapy approach minimizes user fatigue compared to wearable or massage-based devices, while naturally integrating into living environments. Moreover, its emphasis on clinical validation positions it beyond a simple wellness product—allowing it to function as a technological layer that can be integrated into existing healthcare products and services. From sleep solutions and cognitive care programs to elderly care services, Neurélux is increasingly viewed not as a standalone device, but as a platform capable of extending and enhancing existing systems.

Through this trajectory, Korea Lighting delivered a clear message at CES 2026: brain healthcare is no longer a future concept—it is entering everyday reality. At the heart of this shift, Neurélux is opening the door to a new era of daily brain health management, armed with two decisive pillars—non-contact technology and clinical validation.
